title: Google says self-improving AI isn't anywhere close
key_facts: Google DeepMind engineer Haydn Belfield says self-improving AI is far off.
DeepMind has seen no measurable acceleration of AI research driven by AI itself.
AI writes more than 75 percent of production code, but about 88 percent of code changes still need human oversight or review.
The share of code changes fully delegated to AI rose from 7.5 to 11.9 percent.
On the RE-Bench ML engineering benchmark (74 tasks), Argon solves about half, versus 27 percent for Gemini 3.7 Flash.
Gemini capabilities grow about 0.1 General Capability Index points per month with no change in speed.
Over 20 researchers, including Hinton, Bengio and Pachocki, have warned of a possible intelligence explosion.
quote_evidence: Google Deepmind has seen no measurable acceleration of AI research driven by AI itself, according to Belfield.
The team currently rates the risk from AI-driven research automation as low
why_it_matters_hint: A major lab's internal data against the claim that AI is already speeding up AI research.
notes: Belfield's title is given as Google engineer; the article attributes the findings to him and his team.
